To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the child's language is an integral part of his cognitive development.

(1) Children's language behavior is influenced by their cognitive behavior, (2) The influence of cognitive behavior on language behavior is not direct but mediated by the children's social interaction, and (3) The influence of children's cognitive behavior on their language behavior is not uniform.

(1) children's utterances are not random, but are organized according to the same principles as their cognitive behavior, (2) children's utterance organization is based on a set of principles that is different from those underlying the organization of their adult language, (3) children's utter ance organization changes in the direction toward the organization of adult language.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a theory of the acquisition of language, which is based on a genetic epistemological approach.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Piaget's epigenetic theory of intellectual development is a very promising basis of explanation for the acquisition of language.
Piaget's system is not a sufficient but a promising basis for a genetic explanation of language acquisition.

the cognitive principles of assimilation, accommodation, and equilibration can be shown to be antecedents of the linguistic principles of the following functions: (1) the use of words, (2) the acquisition of the meaning of words, (3) the use of syntagms, and (4) the acquisition of grammatical categories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antecedents for the linguistic functions and forms are to be found in the cognitive functions and forms that are described by Piaget's theory.
the Piagetian system provides an excellent theoretical framework for the explanation of the development of the basic functions and forms of language behavior.
the antecedents of linguistic behavior are to be found in the cognitive development of the child.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cognitive antecedents of linguistic phenomena are not necessarily the same for every language.
language is a product of a complex interplay of many different psychological factors, and that it is not possible to reduce language development to any single theory.
language acquisition can be explained by the application of a causal genetic theory of cognitive development.
